recap_lines: A small push flips the answer because the model learned a proxy.
FGSM takes one step, and tiny pushes add up across many inputs.
White-box, black-box and transfer attacks differ in what the attacker has.
Every defense has a limit, and an adaptive attack aims at it.
Distribution shift and natural adversarial inputs need no attacker.
A robustness claim names the attack, the budget and what was not tested.
bookends.segment: Name The Attack, Name The Limit
bookends.command: Quiz me on robustness terms. Give me one short case at a time. I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Use adversarial example, distribution shift, natural adversarial, white-box attack, transfer attack, adaptive attack, certified defense, robust accuracy and residual risk disclosure. Hold back the answer until I reply, then correct me in one sentence.
checks: Check: each answer stayed hidden until you named a term.
Check: each correction says why the look-alike term is wrong.
